# The rebuild kit

How to rebuild Faro from this folder and `llms.txt` alone, one stage at a time, and prove each stage works. Each stage has entry criteria (what must be true before it starts), what to build, and exit criteria (what proves it is done). A stage with a **drill** is scored by a harness against the conformance data; an **outline** stage has its criteria written down but nothing to score it yet.

## The stages

| Stage | Builds | Today |
|---|---|---|
| [1. The core rules](stage-1-core-rules.md) | Weeks and plans, a goal’s status, the projection, what a check-in must say, flags and needs attention, and the scorecard: pure functions over the records, with no screens and no database. | Drill ready: the harness scores it |
| [2. The core data and the change engine](stage-2-core-data.md) | Every core record stored, the change log with undo, and the change engine that takes many changes at once and checks them with the stage 1 rules. | Outline: entry and exit criteria, checked by hand; no drill yet |
| [3. The core screens and journeys](stage-3-core-screens.md) | Each core screen with its route, named parts and one main action, so a person can do every core journey. | Outline: entry and exit criteria, checked by hand; no drill yet |
| [4. Module: Spreadsheets](stage-4-module-spreadsheets.md) | Download every goal, plan number, check-in, person and ask as one Excel workbook or a zip of CSV files in the one spreadsheet format, and load a workbook, a zip or one CSV back: every row goes through the change engine (stage 2), is shown before it is saved, and saves all at once or not at all. Tools for it on Data and Goals. | Outline: entry and exit criteria, checked by hand; no drill yet |

**What the kit fully supports today:** stage 1 only. Stage 1 has everything a rebuild needs in this folder: the records it reads, the rules in plain words with worked examples, the conformance data for every goal in every week of the demo workspace (38124 rows in four files), and a harness that runs a rebuild and scores it. One part of stage 1, what a check-in must say, has worked examples but no conformance rows yet, so the harness doesn’t score it.

**What is an outline:** every other stage. Their pages say what to build and what proves it, so a rebuild can start, but the proof is by hand, and each lists the gaps where the kit doesn’t yet hold what a rebuild needs. Each grows a drill as the kit grows (backlog item 8k: every item adds its module’s stage and runs its drill).

## The drill: a fresh session rebuilds a stage from the kit alone

The drill is the test of the kit, not of the rebuild: whatever the session had to guess shows where the kit is short, and goes back into it.

### What the session gets

A scratch folder holding a copy of `spec/` and `llms.txt`, and nothing else from Faro. Node 22 or later is enough to run the harness. The spec links to files in Faro’s repository (`src/…`, `docs/…`, `evals/…`): they are not in the kit. Don’t look for them; when a link is the only place something is said, write it down as a gap.

### Where to write

```
<scratch folder>/
  llms.txt          read only
  spec/             read only: the kit, unchanged
  rebuild/          everything you write goes here
    drill.json      { "stage": 1, "run": "node main.mjs" }   how the harness runs your rebuild
    main.mjs        (or any language: "run" is any command that works in this folder)
    GAPS.md         what you had to guess, and where the kit should have said it
    drill-out/      written by the harness on every run; leave it out of your code
```

### How to score it

From the scratch folder:

```
node spec/rebuild/drill.mjs rebuild
node spec/rebuild/drill.mjs rebuild --files status          one file while you work (status, flags, projection, scorecard)
node spec/rebuild/drill.mjs rebuild --diffs 30              more of the first differences
```

From Faro’s own repository the same harness is `npm run drill -- <rebuild folder>`. It runs `drill.json`’s command, scores the four files it writes, file by file and column by column, prints the first differences (with the week, the goal and the column), and exits 0 only at 100%.

### The rules of the drill

1. Read only `spec/` and `llms.txt`. Nothing from Faro’s repository, its live app or anywhere else.
2. Don’t change `spec/`. Write only under `rebuild/`.
3. The rebuild computes every row from the workspace it is given (the first argument). It never reads the expected CSV files in `spec/conformance/`; the harness hands it a copy of `workspace.json` in a folder of its own.
4. Keep `rebuild/GAPS.md` as you go: each thing you had to guess, what you guessed, whether the score proved it right, and which spec page should have said it. A gap the conformance data settled still counts: the words should have said it.
5. Finish with the harness’s last output and `GAPS.md`.

## Keeping it true

- These pages are made by `npm run spec` (`src/spec/rebuild.ts`); never edit them by hand.
- A module’s stage comes from its `module.json` (`rebuild`: status, what it builds, entry, exit and gaps). CI fails when a module in `src/modules` has no stage here (`scripts/check-rebuild.mjs`).
- The harness is `scripts/drill.mjs`, copied here as `drill.mjs`. CI runs it on Faro’s own rules (`scripts/drill-faro`), which must score 100%.
